question_en: A put option with an exercise price of $75 sells for a premium of $10. At expiration, the put buyer may experience a loss:
explanation_en: The greatest loss a put buyer can experience is the premium paid. If the price of the underlying asset decreased to zero, the put writer would experience a loss of ($0 – $75) + $10 = –$65.

question_en:
Chris Renburg owns the following portfolio of option-free bonds:

| Par value | Full price | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| $3,000,000 | $2,400,000 | 4.625 |
| $3,500,000 | $3,600,000 | 7.322 |
| $1,500,000 | $1,200,000 | 9.300 |
| $8,000,000 | $7,200,000 | |

The duration of Renburg's bond portfolio is closest to:
explanation_en: Portfolio duration is the weighted average of component securities, using full prices: (2,400,000 / 7,200,000) × 4.625 + (3,600,000 / 7,200,000) × 7.322 + (1,200,000 / 7,200,000) × 9.3 = 6.753.

question_en: A firm attempts to gain market share from its competitors by improving its manufacturing efficiency so that it can increase output and reduce the price of its product. This firm's competitive strategy is most accurately described as:
explanation_en: Cost leadership is a competitive strategy in which a firm attempts to become the lowest-cost producer in the industry. This will enable the firm to offer lower prices than its competitors. A differentiation strategy involves making a product distinctive compared to competing products so that customers will be willing to pay a premium price. A competitive strategy is described as defensive if it is used to maintain a firm's market share and offensive if it is used to gain market share.

question_en: The problem of investment managers taking offsetting active positions is most likely addressed by employing:
explanation_en: With a core-satellite approach, a majority of the assets are invested passively (in the "core" portfolio) with a smaller proportion in actively managed "satellite" portfolios. This reduces the likelihood of excessive trading and offsetting active positions.

question_en: Which of the following sources of short-term funding for banks is most likely to have the lowest interest cost?
explanation_en: Typically, banks do not pay interest on customer checking account deposits. A bank that borrows in either the central bank funds market or the interbank market incurs interest costs.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: The convenience yield associated with holding the underlying asset of a derivative is most accurately described as:
option_a: the nonmonetary benets of holding the asset.
option_b: the monetary and nonmonetary benets of holding the asset.
option_c: the monetary and nonmonetary benets of holding the asset, net of its holding costs.
explanation_en: Convenience yield refers to the nonmonetary benefits of holding an asset. An example is being in a position to sell an overvalued asset that is difficult to sell short. Convenience yield does not include monetary benefits such as interest and dividend income. The costs of holding the asset, net of the monetary and nonmonetary benefits of holding it, is referred to as the net cost of carry.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Yield spreads are most likely to widen in a market environment that exhibits:
option_c: lower-than-normal supply of new bond issuance.
explanation_en: Slowing economic growth reduces firm profitability and creditworthiness and causes yield spreads to widen. Higher-than-normal supply of new bonds can cause yield spreads to widen. Yield spreads tend to narrow during expansions when GDP growth rates are high.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following bonds is most likely to have the greatest convexity at a yield to maturity of 3.5%?
explanation_en: Other things equal, convexity is greater for bonds with longer maturities and lower coupon rates.

question_en: The period of time during which a private capital fund will select investments and direct committed capital to them is best described as a:
explanation_en: The drawdown period for a private equity fund is the span of time over which the fund will draw down its committed capital and use it to invest in portfolio companies. Lockup periods and notice periods are related to hedge fund redemptions.

question_en: Enterprise value is most accurately interpreted as the:
option_a: cost to take over a rm.
option_b: fair market value of a rm’s equity.
option_c: market value of a rm’s equity plus the market value of its debt.
explanation_en: Enterprise value equals the market value of a firm's common stock and debt minus its cash and short-term securities. Enterprise value is interpreted as the amount that would be needed to take over a firm.

question_en: A securities exchange is structured as a call market. On that exchange, a stock would trade at:
option_a: any time the market is open.
option_b: one negotiated price that clears the market.
option_c: prices set by auction or by dealer bid-ask quotes.
explanation_en: In a call market, stocks trade at specific times at one price that clears the market for the stock. In continuous markets, trades occur at any time the market is open at prices set by auction or by dealer quotes.

question_en: An investor writes a put option that will expire in six months with an exercise price of 23 when the underlying price is 20. The investor will collect a premium that is:
explanation_en: The option premium at initiation will equal the option's exercise value of 23 – 20 = 3 plus some positive time value.

question_en: An investor who would only sell shares he owns for $58 or more, but would not buy the same shares for more than $53, is exhibiting:
explanation_en: The tendency to value something already owned more than the same thing if it were not already owned is referred to as endowment bias.

question_en: Regulations are most likely to increase market efficiency if they:
option_c: decrease the incidence of arbitrage trading.
explanation_en: Increasing the availability of information is likely to increase market efficiency. Impediments to trading likely decrease market efficiency.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: For an underlying asset with no holding costs or benefits, the no-arbitrage forward price equals:
option_b: the future value of the spot price.
option_c: zero at initiation of a forward contract.
explanation_en: With no costs or benefits to holding the underlying asset, the no-arbitrage forward price is the future value of the spot price, compounded at the risk-free rate over the term of a forward contract.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 3 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Effective duration is the most appropriate measure of interest rate risk when:
option_a: a bond’s credit rating may change signicantly.
option_b: the investor is seeking to minimize a duration gap.
option_c: the path of interest rate changes aects a bond’s cash ows.
explanation_en: For bonds with future cash flows that depend on the path of interest rate changes, such as those with embedded options, effective duration is the most appropriate measure of interest rate risk. A duration gap relative to an investor's horizon is measured using Macaulay duration. The effect of rating changes may be estimated using credit duration.

question_en: A bond indenture states that the source of funds for repayment will be tolls paid by drivers using a highway constructed with the bond proceeds. This bond is most likely a:
explanation_en: Revenue bonds are municipal bonds that will be repaid from revenues generated by a specific project such as a toll road. Secured bonds have specific assets pledged as collateral. Quasi-government entities are agencies created by sovereign governments.
